os_version: macOS 26.5.2 (25F84), Apple Silicon, live user session

stack_detection.method: AX tree responds; AXWebArea node present under the window
stack_detection.signature: AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid) answers, but see notes: content is LAZY — first shallow probe returned 72 nodes of window chrome only (page text absent)

channel_setup: Same Accessibility TCC grant as all AX cells. No app-side flag needed, but Chrome populates web-content accessibility ON DEMAND: the tree was a stub (window chrome only, 'Dupont'/'Customer name' absent) until sustained AX querying flagged an assistive client; a later probe then returned the full page (200 nodes incl. all table text and buttons). AXUIElementSetAttributeValue(app,'AXEnhancedUserInterface',true) itself returned error -25208, yet content appeared anyway after repeated deep queries.

t1_read_text.detail: After warm-up: page text (Orders, Dupont SARL, Ship, Customer name) present in the AX tree as real strings. BEFORE warm-up the same query honestly returned a near-empty web area — explicit emptiness, not wrong content.

t2_enumerate.detail: Buttons/links/fields exposed with AXFrame rects once populated (200 nodes, 19.8 KB, 54 ms). Frames are in GLOBAL screen points (window at its real position) — directly clickable, unlike CDP device-pixel boxes.

t3_live_value.detail: Not separately re-run on this channel (T3 done via CDP on the same instance); AX exposes AXValue on the input and there is no reason to expect divergence, but unmeasured = unclaimed.

t4_living_screen.detail: Not measured on this channel (measured on CDP for the same app). AX would require polling or AXObserver notifications; cost expected higher than CDP diffs.

t5_blind_action.detail: Not re-run via AX (proven on TextEdit cell for AX-coordinate clicking, and via CDP for this app).

t6_pictorial.detail: The canvas page exposes an AXWebArea whose canvas region carries no fabricated text — consistent with CDP's declared opaque rect.

measurements.notes: Full-depth AX walk of the populated page = 19.8 KB / ~4950 tokens — 15× heavier than the 1.3 KB distilled CDP view of the SAME screen, because AX nests every DOM group. An unbounded deep walk on the UNPOPULATED tree earlier cost >60 s (lazy population + per-attribute IPC round-trips): bound your walks. Two-channel lesson: for a Chromium app, CDP is the cheap semantic channel when you control the launch; AX is the no-flags fallback that also sees browser-chrome overlays (the Google Translate popup was in the AX window, invisible to CDP).

runtime_verification.method: String probes (Orders/Dupont/Customer name/Ship) against the AX serialization, cross-checked with the native window screenshot and the CDP view of the same instant.
runtime_verification.agreement: Agreement after population; before population the web area was explicitly (near-)empty — a predictability wrinkle, not a divergence: at no point did AX return content that contradicted the screen.
